content:
maya: hey—noticed a bunch of user reports of duplicate token charges in the console after streaming reconnects. reproducer: client times out mid-stream, reconnects, same request continues, tool call fires twice, console shows two provisional charges and only one later gets reconciled :confused:

oscar: ugh. do we know whether the extra provisional charge is from duplicate toolcall attribution or from disconnected suffix being re-counted? any traces? @billing-bot can you dump a sample ledger trace?

billing-bot: ledger-event: session=sess_9a2f, request=rid_77, provisional_charge=120, confirmed_charge=80, reconcile_status=pending

maya: attached a short trace: router forwarded same client-id on reconnect but session-id changed because of our ephemeral handoff. toolcall had no idempotency token. looks like runtime accepted both tool invocations.

samir: proposed fix: require a stable stream-session-id propagated across reconnects and use that as instrumenting key for the ledger. if reconnect sees the same session-id, it should graft onto existing provisional state instead of creating a fresh provisional entry.

izzy: small UX ask: even if we fix server-side, console should display "provisional" vs "confirmed" credits per request and allow a hover explanation. customers keep pinging support thinking they were billed twice.

ruth: internal-api debate: do we (A) change router to keep session-id sticky across handoffs (risky), (B) make runtime dedupe on toolcall idempotency-key (requires client SDK changes), or (C) adopt a settle_stream(rid, final_ack_token) endpoint that the runtime calls when stream completes to reconcile provisional -> confirmed? tradeoffs? :thinking_face: 

oscar: C seems low-risk to deploy from runtime side but pushes complexity into our billing pipeline and needs strong ordering guarantees. we already have provisional vs confirmed concept downstream, but settle_stream would need idempotency and retries itself.

samir: also need to handle truncation. if the client or network truncates an unfinished chunk we currently mark those tokens provisional and let a grace window expire. if the client reconnects and resumes mid-prefix, attribution gets messy because prefix tokens were already credited to old provisional entry.

maya: example logs from reproducer:
```
INFO router: client_id=cli_123, session=new, session_prev=sess_9a2f, forwarded_to=node-3
INFO runtime: start_stream req=rid_77, toolcall_id=tool_x
WARN client: timeout at chunk 42, connection closed
INFO router: reconnect req=rid_77, client_id=cli_123, new_session=sess_9b0
INFO runtime: start_stream req=rid_77, toolcall_id=tool_x (no idempotency)
```

izzy: can we do a hybrid? settle_stream + require runtime to include origin_session in settle call. settle call could accept an array of provisional ids to merge. then billing pipeline merges duplicates and emits a single confirmed charge.

ruth: we must be careful about race with retries: settle_stream might arrive before duplicate provisional is created or after. ledger merge must be commutative and idempotent.

oscar: implementation sketch: add header X-Stream-Session, require SDKs propagate session token. router keeps session sticky for 30s and forwards header. runtime creates provisional entries keyed by (session_token, provisional_nonce). settle_stream API:
```
POST /internal/billing/settle_stream
{ "session": "sess_9a2f", "request": "rid_77", "confirmed_tokens": 80, "provisional_ids": ["p_432","p_433"] }
``
response 200 ok | 409 merge-in-progress
```

samir: test plan: unit tests for ledger merge, e2e with flaky network sim (close mid-stream, reconnect), and console smoke showing provisional -> confirmed transition animation. add telemetry counter: provisional_merge_rate.

maya: sounds good. I'll spin up a tiny RFC doc but wanted quick alignment here before I draft. any objections to settling on settle_stream + session header hybrid?

oscar: +1 from infra. samir? izzy? ruth?

samir: +1

izzy: +1 — will open console PR for provisional badge copy

ruth: +1 — will add ledger constraints and propose throttle/timeout for merge window

billing-bot: automation: created ticket BILL-8312 linking runtime settle_stream API and console UX

maya: thanks all. I'll draft RFC and ping eng-runtime + billing for review. :party_parrot:
